# Global Customer Due Diligence Policy

Document ID: MGB-KYC-POL-001 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-03-01 | Owner: Group Financial Crime Compliance | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy sets the minimum customer due diligence (CDD) standards for all clients of the Corporate & Investment Banking (CIB) division of Meridian Global Bank (MGB). It applies to every booking jurisdiction unless a jurisdiction addendum sets a stricter or more specific requirement, in which case the addendum prevails for clients booked in that jurisdiction.

The policy covers new client onboarding, periodic review, event-driven review and exit. It must be read together with the UBO Identification Standard (MGB-KYC-STD-011), the PEP Standard (MGB-KYC-STD-012) and the Enhanced Due Diligence Standard (MGB-KYC-STD-013).

## 2. Roles and responsibilities

- Relationship Managers (RMs) own the client relationship and collect information and documents from the client.
- Onboarding Operations performs the KYC review as maker and the quality check as checker, applying the four-eyes principle.
- CIB Compliance advises on high-risk cases and approves cases where this policy or a standard requires it.
- Group Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) owns this policy and its interpretation.

## 3. Client identification

Every client must be identified and verified before any account is opened or any transaction is processed. Verification uses reliable, independent documents. Identity documents must be unexpired at the time of verification. The detailed document checklist by entity type is set out in the CIB Client Onboarding Procedure (MGB-KYC-PROC-010).

## 4. Risk rating and periodic review

### 4.1 Client risk rating

Each client receives a risk score from 1 to 100 at onboarding and at every review. The score combines five factors: client type, jurisdiction, products used, delivery channel and ownership complexity. The score maps to a risk rating as shown in Table 1.

| Risk rating | Score range | Typical characteristics |
|---|---|---|
| Low | 40 or below | Listed or regulated entity, simple ownership, low-risk jurisdiction |
| Medium | 41 to 70 | Private company, moderate ownership complexity, standard products |
| High | 71 or above | Complex ownership, high-risk jurisdiction nexus, PEP involvement or cash-intensive activity |

### 4.2 Periodic review cycles

Clients must be fully reviewed and their KYC refreshed at the frequency set by their risk rating, as shown in Table 2. The review date is calculated from the date of the last completed review.

| Risk rating | KYC refresh frequency | Review approver |
|---|---|---|
| High | Every 12 months | Country Head of Compliance |
| Medium | Every 24 months | Onboarding Operations checker |
| Low | Every 36 months | Onboarding Operations checker |

Jurisdiction addenda may set a shorter cycle for clients booked in that jurisdiction. Where they do, the addendum cycle applies.

### 4.3 Overdue reviews

A review not completed within 30 days after its due date is overdue. Overdue High-risk reviews are reported weekly to the Country Head of CIB, and new transactions for the client require Compliance approval until the review is completed.

### 4.4 Trigger events

Certain events require an out-of-cycle review, which must be completed within 30 calendar days of the event becoming known, regardless of when the next scheduled review is due. Trigger events are:

- a change of ultimate beneficial owner;
- an adverse media hit assessed as material;
- a true sanctions match on the client or a related party;
- a change in the client's jurisdiction of incorporation;
- an Unusual Activity Report (UAR) raised on the client.

## 5. Record keeping

All CDD records, including documents, screening results and approvals, must be retained for at least seven years after the end of the client relationship.

# UK KYC Addendum

Document ID: MGB-KYC-ADD-UK | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-03-01 | Owner: UK Financial Crime Compliance | Jurisdiction: UK

## 1. Application

This addendum applies to all CIB clients booked in the United Kingdom. It supplements the Global Customer Due Diligence Policy (MGB-KYC-POL-001). Where this addendum is silent, the global policy applies.

## 2. Persons with significant control (PSC)

For UK-incorporated clients, Onboarding Operations must check the Companies House register of persons with significant control (PSC) and compare it with the ownership information provided by the client.

Any discrepancy between the PSC register and the client-provided ownership must be reported to Onboarding Compliance within 5 business days of identification. The case may not be approved until Onboarding Compliance has recorded its assessment of the discrepancy.

## 3. Periodic review

UK clients follow the global periodic review cycles. No UK-specific cycle applies.

# Singapore KYC Addendum

Document ID: MGB-KYC-ADD-SG | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-03-01 | Owner: Singapore Financial Crime Compliance | Jurisdiction: SG

## 1. Application

This addendum applies to all CIB clients booked in Singapore and supplements the Global Customer Due Diligence Policy (MGB-KYC-POL-001).

## 2. Beneficial ownership for high-risk clients

For clients rated High risk and booked in Singapore, the threshold for identifying ultimate beneficial owners is lowered from 25% to 10%. Every natural person holding 10% or more of ownership or control must be identified and verified. The global threshold of 25% continues to apply to Low and Medium risk clients.

## 3. Corporate documents

A current business profile from the Singapore registry, dated within the last 30 days, must be obtained for every Singapore-incorporated client at onboarding and at each periodic review.

## 4. Periodic review

Singapore clients follow the global periodic review cycles.

# Hong Kong KYC Addendum

Document ID: MGB-KYC-ADD-HK | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-03-01 | Owner: Hong Kong Financial Crime Compliance | Jurisdiction: HK

## 1. Application

This addendum applies to all CIB clients booked in Hong Kong and supplements the Global Customer Due Diligence Policy (MGB-KYC-POL-001).

## 2. Certification of corporate documents

For Hong Kong-incorporated clients, certified true copies of the Business Registration Certificate and the Certificate of Incorporation are required. Certification may be performed by MGB staff who have seen the original, by a certified public accountant, or by a solicitor.

## 3. Periodic review

Medium-risk clients booked in Hong Kong must be reviewed every 18 months. This overrides the global cycle for Medium-risk clients. High-risk and Low-risk clients follow the global cycles.

## 4. Trigger events

Trigger events under section 4.4 of the global policy apply in full to Hong Kong clients.

# UAE KYC Addendum

Document ID: MGB-KYC-ADD-AE | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-03-01 | Owner: UAE Financial Crime Compliance | Jurisdiction: AE

## 1. Application

This addendum applies to all CIB clients booked in the United Arab Emirates and supplements the Global Customer Due Diligence Policy (MGB-KYC-POL-001).

## 2. Trade licence

A copy of the client's valid trade licence must be obtained at onboarding. The trade licence must have at least 90 days of remaining validity on the date of onboarding. A licence expiring sooner must be renewed before the case can be approved.

## 3. Free-zone entities

Clients incorporated in a UAE free zone whose business is cash-intensive are rated High risk by default. In addition to the 12-month KYC refresh, their transaction activity must be reviewed every 6 months against the expected activity recorded at onboarding.

## 4. Periodic review

Other UAE clients follow the global periodic review cycles.

# CIB Client Onboarding Procedure

Document ID: MGB-KYC-PROC-010 | Version: 2025.2 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-05-01 | Owner: CIB Onboarding Operations | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes how CIB clients are onboarded, from first contact to account activation. It implements the Global Customer Due Diligence Policy (MGB-KYC-POL-001) and the CIB Onboarding Service Level Standard (MGB-OPS-STD-050).

## 2. Onboarding flow

Every onboarding case moves through eight steps. Steps 5 and 6 must be performed by different people (four-eyes principle).

1. RM intake: the RM records the client, products and expected activity.
2. Document collection: the RM collects the documents listed in Table 3.
3. Screening: sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening on the client and all related parties.
4. Risk rating: the client risk score is calculated (see MGB-KYC-POL-001 section 4.1).
5. KYC review (maker): Onboarding Operations reviews documents and screening results.
6. Quality check (checker): a second analyst checks the maker's work.
7. Approval: by the approver required for the risk rating and any PEP or EDD conditions.
8. Account activation: accounts are opened and the RM is notified.

## 3. Rework

If the checker or approver finds missing or incorrect information, the case is returned to the RM. Every return counts as a rework loop and means the case is not first-time-right.

## 4. Document checklist

Table 3 lists the minimum documents by entity type. Proof of address must be no more than 3 months old. Identity documents must be unexpired.

| Entity type | Corporate documents | Ownership and control | Simplified treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Private limited company | Certificate of incorporation; constitution; registry extract | Shareholder register; identify UBOs at 25% | No |
| Listed company (approved exchange) | Certificate of incorporation; evidence of listing | Confirm listing only; no further UBO identification | Yes |
| Partnership | Partnership agreement; registration | Identify all partners with 25% or more | No |
| Trust | Trust deed | Settlor, trustees, protector, beneficiaries (see MGB-KYC-STD-011) | No |
| Special purpose vehicle | Incorporation documents; structure chart | Look through to UBOs; structure chart mandatory | No |
| Government entity | Evidence of government ownership | Not applicable | Yes, if Low risk |

## 5. Screening

Screening covers the client, its directors, its UBOs and authorised signatories. Potential matches are handled under the Sanctions Compliance Policy (MGB-SAN-POL-020).

# Ultimate Beneficial Owner Identification Standard

Document ID: MGB-KYC-STD-011 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-03-01 | Owner: Group Financial Crime Compliance | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose

This standard defines how MGB identifies and verifies the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of CIB clients.

## 2. Definitions

An ultimate beneficial owner is a natural person who ultimately owns or controls the client.

## 3. Ownership and control threshold

Any natural person who holds, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of the ownership or voting rights of the client is a UBO. Any natural person who otherwise exercises control over the client, for example through the right to appoint the majority of the board, is also a UBO regardless of shareholding. Jurisdiction addenda may set a lower threshold.

## 4. Trusts

For trusts and similar legal arrangements, identify and verify the settlor, all trustees, any protector, every beneficiary with an interest of 25% or more, and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control over the trust.

## 5. Layered ownership

Where there are more than three layers of legal entities between the client and its UBO, the structure is considered complex and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies under MGB-KYC-STD-013. A structure chart signed by the client is mandatory.

## 6. Nominee arrangements

Nominee shareholders and directors must be disclosed. The person on whose behalf the nominee acts must be identified as if they held the interest directly.

# Politically Exposed Persons Standard

Document ID: MGB-KYC-STD-012 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-03-01 | Owner: Group Financial Crime Compliance | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose

This standard sets out how MGB identifies and manages relationships involving politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates.

## 2. Identification

PEP screening is performed at onboarding, at every periodic review and in the daily batch rescreen. A client is PEP-connected if a director, UBO or authorised signatory is a PEP.

## 3. Approval

Onboarding a domestic PEP-connected client requires approval by the Country Head of Compliance. Onboarding a foreign PEP-connected client requires approval by the Group Head of Financial Crime Compliance (FCC). PEP-connected clients are rated High risk and are subject to EDD.

## 4. Ongoing monitoring

PEP-connected clients are reviewed every 12 months, in line with the High-risk cycle.

## 5. Declassification

A person may be declassified as a PEP no earlier than 24 months after leaving the public function, subject to a documented Compliance assessment of residual risk.

# Enhanced Due Diligence Standard

Document ID: MGB-KYC-STD-013 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-03-01 | Owner: Group Financial Crime Compliance | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose

This standard defines when Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies and what it requires.

## 2. EDD triggers

EDD applies when any of the following is true:

- the client is rated High risk;
- a director, UBO or signatory is a PEP;
- there are more than three ownership layers between the client and its UBO;
- the client has a nexus to a Tier 2 jurisdiction on the Restricted and High-Risk Jurisdictions List (MGB-SAN-LST-021);
- the client's business is cash-intensive;
- material adverse media has been identified.

## 3. EDD requirements

EDD cases require documentary evidence of the source of wealth (SoW) of each UBO and the source of funds (SoF) for the expected activity, enhanced ongoing monitoring, and senior approval as set out in section 5. A site visit is required for High-risk clients with a Tier 2 jurisdiction nexus.

## 4. Prohibited structures

Bearer shares are prohibited unless they are immobilised with an MGB-approved custodian. A client with bearer shares that are not immobilised may not be onboarded.

## 5. Approval

EDD cases require dual approval by the Country Head of Compliance and the Country Head of CIB.

# Sanctions Compliance Policy

Document ID: MGB-SAN-POL-020 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Owner: Group Sanctions | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose

This policy ensures MGB does not deal with sanctioned persons, entities, vessels or jurisdictions, and complies with all applicable sanctions regimes.

## 2. Scope

The policy applies to all CIB clients, transactions and staff in every booking jurisdiction.

## 3. Screening

Screening is performed at client onboarding, on every trade finance transaction, and in a daily batch rescreen of the full client base against updated sanctions lists.

## 4. Potential matches

Every potential match generated by screening must be dispositioned within 24 hours. The analyst must record the reasons for discounting a match or escalate it as a possible true match.

## 5. True matches

When a true match is confirmed, all processing must stop immediately. The case must be escalated to Group Sanctions Advisory within 2 hours. Staff must not inform the client or any third party of the match or the escalation (no tipping off).

## 6. Restricted jurisdictions

Business involving jurisdictions on the Restricted and High-Risk Jurisdictions List (MGB-SAN-LST-021) is prohibited or subject to EDD, according to the tier of the jurisdiction.

# Restricted and High-Risk Jurisdictions List

Document ID: MGB-SAN-LST-021 | Version: 2025.3 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-07-01 | Owner: Group Sanctions | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

This list is maintained by Group Sanctions and reviewed quarterly. Tier 1 jurisdictions are prohibited: no new business and no transactions. Tier 2 jurisdictions are high-risk: business is permitted only with EDD under MGB-KYC-STD-013.

| Tier | Jurisdiction or region | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | Iran | Prohibited |
| Tier 1 | North Korea | Prohibited |
| Tier 1 | Syria | Prohibited |
| Tier 1 | Cuba | Prohibited |
| Tier 1 | Crimea region | Prohibited |
| Tier 2 | Myanmar | EDD required |
| Tier 2 | Afghanistan | EDD required |
| Tier 2 | Yemen | EDD required |
| Tier 2 | Venezuela | EDD required |
| Tier 2 | Belarus | EDD required |

# Trade Sanctions Screening Procedure

Document ID: MGB-SAN-PROC-022 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Owner: Group Sanctions | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose

This procedure sets out how Trade Operations screens trade finance transactions for sanctions risk.

## 2. What to screen

Every trade transaction must screen all parties and elements: the applicant, the beneficiary, all banks in the transaction, the vessel by its IMO number, the ports of loading, transhipment and discharge, the shipping line and carrier, and the goods description against the dual-use goods list.

## 3. Timing

Screening is performed on receipt of the transaction and again on any amendment that adds or changes a party, vessel, port or goods description.

## 4. Vessel red flags

A gap of more than 24 hours in the vessel's AIS (automatic identification system) transmissions during the past 12 months is a red flag. Other red flags include recent changes of flag or name and ship-to-ship transfers in high-risk waters. Any red flag must be escalated to Sanctions before the transaction proceeds.

## 5. Escalation

Escalations are handled under sections 4 and 5 of the Sanctions Compliance Policy (MGB-SAN-POL-020).

# Trade Finance Policy

Document ID: MGB-TF-POL-030 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-02-01 | Owner: Global Trade | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose

This policy governs the trade finance products MGB offers to CIB clients and the limits within which they may be provided.

## 2. Products

- Import and export letters of credit (LCs), sight and usance
- Standby letters of credit (SBLCs) and bank guarantees
- Documentary collections
- Supply chain finance

## 3. Credit

All trade products require an approved trade line under the CIB Credit Delegated Authority Matrix (MGB-CR-MAT-040).

## 4. Tenor limits

The maximum tenor for a usance LC is 360 days. Any longer tenor requires Credit Committee approval in addition to the approved trade line.

## 5. Operational standards

Document examination, discrepancy handling and waivers follow the Documentary Credit Examination Procedure (MGB-TF-PROC-031) and the Trade Discrepancy Waiver Approval Matrix (MGB-TF-MAT-032).

# Documentary Credit Examination Procedure

Document ID: MGB-TF-PROC-031 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-04-01 | Owner: Global Trade Operations | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose

This procedure sets out how Trade Operations examines documents presented under documentary credits (DCs).

## 2. Standard of examination

Documents are examined on their face for compliance with the terms of the credit and with the international rules referenced in the credit. This procedure refers to those rules by name only and does not restate them.

## 3. Timeline

MGB's internal target is to complete examination within 3 banking days of presentation. This is inside the maximum of 5 banking days allowed under the international rules.

## 4. Common discrepancies

| Discrepancy | Typical cause | First action |
|---|---|---|
| Late presentation | Documents presented after the presentation period | Notify applicant; seek waiver |
| Description of goods | Invoice description differs from the credit | Notify applicant; check sanctions relevance |
| Port mismatch | Bill of lading port differs from the credit | Escalate to Sanctions; do not seek waiver |
| Missing document | A required document was not presented | Notify presenter |
| Amount exceeded | Invoice exceeds credit amount or tolerance | Notify applicant; seek waiver |

## 5. Waivers

Waivers of discrepancies are approved under the Trade Discrepancy Waiver Approval Matrix (MGB-TF-MAT-032).

# Trade Discrepancy Waiver Approval Matrix

Document ID: MGB-TF-MAT-032 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-04-01 | Owner: Global Trade Operations | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

This matrix sets out who may approve the waiver of discrepancies in documents presented under documentary credits. Amounts are the USD equivalent of the drawing.

| Over (USD) | Up to and including (USD) | Primary approver | Concurrence | Conditions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1,000,000 | Trade Operations Team Lead | Not required | Applicant written consent required (a) |
| 1,000,000 | 5,000,000 | Country Head of Trade Operations | Not required | Applicant written consent required (a) |
| 5,000,000 | 20,000,000 | Regional Head of Trade Operations | Credit Risk (b) | Applicant written consent required (a) |
| 20,000,000 | No limit | Global Head of Trade | CRO delegate | Applicant written consent required (a) |

(a) The applicant's written consent to waive the discrepancies is required in every case, regardless of amount.

(b) Credit Risk concurrence is provided by the Senior Credit Officer covering the client, as set out in MGB-CR-MAT-040.

Waivers are not permitted for discrepancies in sanctions-relevant data, including ports, vessel and goods description. These must be escalated to Sanctions under MGB-SAN-PROC-022.

# SBLC and Guarantee Issuance Procedure

Document ID: MGB-TF-PROC-033 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-02-01 | Owner: Global Trade Operations | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose

This procedure covers the issuance of standby letters of credit (SBLCs) and bank guarantees for CIB clients.

## 2. Standard wording

MGB maintains standard templates for SBLCs and guarantees. Use of a standard template with no changes requires only Trade Operations checker approval.

## 3. Non-standard wording and evergreen clauses

Any non-standard wording requires review by Legal before issuance. An evergreen or auto-extension clause, under which the instrument renews automatically unless cancelled, requires approval by both Legal and Credit, and the instrument must carry a final expiry date no more than 5 years from issuance.

## 4. Claims

Claims are examined within 3 banking days. Claims under SBLCs are checked against the sanctions screening requirements in MGB-SAN-PROC-022 before payment.

# Trade-Based Money Laundering Red Flags Guide

Document ID: MGB-TF-GDE-034 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-03-01 | Owner: Group Financial Crime Compliance | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose

This guide helps Trade Operations and RMs recognise indicators of trade-based money laundering (TBML).

## 2. Pricing red flags

An invoice price that varies by more than 25% from the market benchmark for the goods is a red flag for over- or under-invoicing.

## 3. Shipping red flags

- Shipping routes that make no commercial sense for the goods
- Transhipment through jurisdictions with weak controls
- Goods inconsistent with the client's stated business

## 4. Documentary red flags

- Repeated amendments to beneficiary or goods description
- Third-party payments with no clear rationale

## 5. What to do

If you identify a red flag, raise an Unusual Activity Report (UAR) to Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) within 1 business day. Do not discuss your concern with the client.

# Documentary Collections Procedure

Document ID: MGB-TF-PROC-035 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-02-01 | Owner: Global Trade Operations | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose

This procedure covers export and import documentary collections handled by MGB.

## 2. Types of collection

Under documents against payment (D/P), documents are released only when the drawee pays. Under documents against acceptance (D/A), documents are released when the drawee accepts a bill of exchange.

## 3. Release and follow-up

Documents may be released against acceptance only on the client's written instruction. While a collection remains unpaid, a tracer must be sent to the collecting bank every 30 days.

# Supply Chain Finance Product Guide

Document ID: MGB-TF-GDE-036 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-06-01 | Owner: Global Trade | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## Supply Chain Finance Product Guide

Meridian Global Bank, Global Trade. For CIB RMs and Trade Operations.

## What is supply chain finance?

MGB pays the supplier early against an invoice approved by the buyer. The buyer repays MGB at the invoice due date.

## Who it is for

- Large corporate buyers with many suppliers
- Suppliers who want faster cash
- Buyers who want to extend payment terms

## Key parameters

| Parameter | Limit |
|---|---|
| Maximum financing | 90% of approved invoice value |
| Maximum tenor | 180 days |
| Eligible buyers | MGB internal grade 1 to 6 |

## Eligibility

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Buyer grade | 1 to 6 on the MGB internal scale |
| Invoice status | Approved by the buyer |
| Supplier KYC | Completed under MGB-KYC-POL-001 |

## How a programme is set up

1. Credit approval of the buyer trade line
2. Programme agreement signed
3. Suppliers onboarded
4. Invoices uploaded and financed

## Pricing

Discount margin over the reference rate, based on the buyer's grade and tenor.

## Risks

- Dilution: invoices reduced after financing
- Fraud: fictitious invoices
- Concentration on one buyer

## Controls

Invoices are checked against TBML indicators in MGB-TF-GDE-034.

## Contacts

Global Trade product team.

# CIB Onboarding Service Level Standard

Document ID: MGB-OPS-STD-050 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-03-01 | Owner: CIB Onboarding Operations | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

## 1. Purpose

This standard defines the service levels for CIB client onboarding and how they are measured.

## 2. Turnaround time (TAT)

The onboarding TAT target is 10 business days for Low and Medium risk clients and 20 business days for High risk clients. The TAT clock starts when a complete document pack has been received. The clock pauses while the case is waiting for information from the client and restarts when the information is received.

## 3. First-time-right (FTR)

A case is first-time-right when it is approved without any rework loop back to the RM. The FTR target is 85% of cases each month.

## 4. Account activation

Accounts must be activated within 1 business day of KYC approval.

## 5. Reporting

TAT and FTR are reported monthly by country to the Country Head of CIB.

# Onboarding FAQ for Relationship Managers

Document ID: MGB-FAQ-060 | Version: 2024.2 | Status: current | Effective: 2024-06-10 | Owner: CIB Onboarding Operations | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

### How long does onboarding take?
Most low and medium risk clients are onboarded within two weeks once we have everything we need. High risk clients take about four weeks.

### How often will my client be reviewed?
High risk clients are reviewed every year. Medium risk clients are reviewed every three years, and low risk clients every five years.

### My client is listed on a stock exchange. Do we still need ownership details?
If the exchange is on our approved list, we only need evidence of the listing.

### Can I start a transaction before onboarding is finished?
No. No account can be opened and no transaction processed until onboarding is approved.

### What happens if my client's documents are old?
Proof of address must be recent, and identity documents must not have expired. Ask the client for new copies.

Up to 360 days without extra approval.

# Policy Change Bulletin, February 2025

Document ID: MGB-COM-063 | Version: 2025.1 | Status: current | Effective: 2025-02-17 | Owner: Group Financial Crime Compliance | Jurisdiction: GLOBAL

To: all CIB staff. From: Group Financial Crime Compliance and Global Trade Operations. Date: 17 February 2025.

## Changes to KYC periodic review cycles

From 1 March 2025, version 2025.1 of the Global Customer Due Diligence Policy changes the periodic review cycles. Medium-risk clients move from every 36 months to every 24 months. Low-risk clients move from every 60 months to every 36 months. High-risk clients remain at every 12 months.

## Changes to discrepancy waiver authorities

From 1 April 2025, version 2025.1 of the Trade Discrepancy Waiver Approval Matrix revises the approval bands and introduces Credit Risk concurrence for waivers over USD 5 million up to USD 20 million.

## What you need to do

Read the updated documents on the policy portal. Reviews already scheduled will be re-dated automatically.
